A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RegCache research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v4.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification and retrieval experiments, outlier measurements, ablations and computational-efficiency results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 reports original vision-encoder experiments and adds VLM, segmentation, latency and method-variant results, including Tables 4, 6 and 11–15.

M1.justification: The core curating, KV-caching and token-deletion procedure remains unchanged. v4 adds bounded variants: reconstruction-MSE selection of prefix/deletion counts, replacement of deleted tokens by spatial interpolation for segmentation, and FP16 token processing instead of deletion (Appendices K, H and L).

E1.justification: v4 adds image question answering on GQA and VQAv2, video understanding on Video-MME and MLVU, and semantic segmentation on ADE20K. Classification coverage also expands to Caltech101, Oxford-IIIT Pet and DTD. These introduce substantially different tasks and input conditions beyond the retained classification and retrieval evaluations.

E2.justification: ERQ is newly evaluated in the ImageNet-1k and MS-COCO comparisons, and SmoothQuant becomes an evaluated comparator in Appendix P rather than merely a citation. FIMA-Q, QuaRot and test-time registers were already evaluated in v3; their relocation does not constitute new baselines.

E3.justification: Retrieval evaluation adds W4A4 for the previously W6A6/W8A8-only baselines and removes R@5 reporting; FIMA-Q already had W4A4 results. New VLM and segmentation experiments introduce additional configurations and metrics. v3's whole-validation-set timing and FLOPs evaluation is replaced by TensorRT/A6000 latency measurements, including batch-64 standalone encoders and VLM prefill timing. These timing results are not directly comparable across versions. AWQ evaluation also narrows from four encoders to CLIP.

E4.justification: New analyses test label-free reconstruction-based selection, FP16 retention versus token deletion, sink/random/non-sink segmentation behavior, spatial interpolation, and transfer of SmoothQuant to vision encoders (Appendices H, K, L and P). The original caching/deletion ablation, insertion-layer sensitivity and tokenization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same cosine-similarity means and ± values. Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests; the added result tables continue point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: v4 adds extensive VLM, segmentation, ERQ, SmoothQuant and variant results, while removing R@5, three encoders' AWQ results and the old FLOPs/timing entries. Existing values also change: Table 2's SigLIP2 PTQ4ViT+RegCache W6A6 accuracy changes from 68.17 to 69.02. FIMA-Q classification results are reassigned between CLIP/OpenCLIP, resolving v3 Table 8's inconsistent labels. A new inconsistency appears: v4 Table 2 reports a SigLIP W6A6 best gain of 3.38, although its PTQ4ViT rows imply 3.70.

T1.justification: Lemma 1 and its proof, including Equations (3)–(6), are mathematically unchanged between v3 Appendix B and v4 Appendix F. The principal method definitions in Equations (1)–(2) also remain unchanged; the new variants do not introduce new formal theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction elevate particularly strong 4-bit benefits into the headline claims, and the introduction explicitly distinguishes the motivating observations from behavior in smaller ViTs. The central contribution—training-free outlier mitigation through universal middle-layer prefixes and token deletion—remains intact.

C2.justification: v4 substantially extends applicability and deployment interpretations: reconstruction-based selection reduces dependence on labeled validation, interpolation supports dense prediction, and FP16 retention trades accuracy for a computational bottleneck. Section 5.4 adds an interpretation of vision-encoder bottlenecks after LLM acceleration, while Appendix P contrasts SmoothQuant with vision-specific quantization. The original outlier-emergence explanation and stated hyperparameter-tuning limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly specifies PTQ4ViT/ERQ calibration counts and FIMA-Q optimization/calibration budgets, and gives more specific GPU assignments, including A100 80GB hardware. Table 6 documents TensorRT, A6000 hardware and standalone batch size. These improve documentation; newly disclosed budgets do not establish changes to previously conducted experiments.

R1.justification: v4 expands positioning toward VLM deployment and efficiency through Qwen3-VL, LLaVA, FastVLM and related literature, alongside ERQ and new benchmark references. Related work adds a dedicated outlier-control comparison and clarifies the relationship to training-free, concurrent test-time registers. Several earlier references, including APHQ-ViT, DOPQ-ViT and the robotics/survey motivation, are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and substantial explanatory passages are rewritten. Experiments are reorganized into setup, main results, analyses, latency and other experiments; the appendices are extensively reordered, with some material moved into the main text. These are substantial narrative changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v3 Figure 1 is reworked into a PTQ-pipeline overview and a separate sink-token schematic. FIMA-Q results are consolidated into enlarged benchmark tables, retrieval tables are redesigned, and new VLM, latency and analysis tables are added. Appendix figures and tables are extensively relocated and repaginated.

improvement.justification: v4 addresses important gaps in v3's practical validation: VLM image/video experiments and TensorRT measurements directly support deployment relevance, while segmentation and label-free selection tests address spatial-output and supervision constraints (Tables 4, 6, 11–14). These substantially strengthen evidence for the method's applicability. Removing R@5 and most AWQ results reduces retained evidence, and the new Table 2 summary inconsistency weakens reporting accuracy, but these drawbacks do not outweigh the gains in validation of central claims.
